rows.text: Vivi is a ritual that grows. Every noncreature spell puts a counter on him and pings each opponent, and once per turn he taps for mana equal to his power. So the turn works in one direction: cast the free and cheap spells first to grow him, THEN activate for a pile of mana, then spend it. Get the order wrong and you have used the deck's biggest mana source at half size.

rows.name: Vivi Ornitier
rows.text: {0}: add mana equal to his power, once each turn on your turn. Every noncreature spell you cast grows him by one and deals one to each opponent, so the damage and the mana scale together.
Note the activation is once per turn and only on your turn. Count your hand before you use it — three cantrips first turns a four-mana activation into a seven-mana one.

rows.name: Harmonic Prodigy
rows.text: Vivi is a Wizard, so his cast trigger fires TWICE. Two counters and two damage to each opponent per spell.

rows.name: Hexing Squelcher
rows.text: your spells cannot be countered and your creatures all get ward, which is what protects a storm turn from a blue table.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep cheap spells and one mana source, not a hand of expensive payoffs. This deck wins by chaining six or eight spells in a turn, and Vivi turns that chain into both mana and damage.
Sequence for Vivi's power. Cast every zero- and one-mana spell you can before the {0} activation, because you only get one per turn and its size is locked in when you use it.

rows.name: Harmonic Prodigy
rows.text: two mana that doubles the commander. Prioritise it over almost any other two-drop.

rows.name: Niv-Mizzet, Parun
rows.text: six specific pips is a real cost. He is not the plan on turn five; he is the finisher once Vivi has already made the mana.
